newsitem.title: UK: Parasites found in ancient South American mummies.
newsitem.headline: Parasites found in ancient South American mummies.

text.p: Colombian researchers said on Friday they had found evidence of a deadly parasite in 4,000-year-old mummies from Peru.
Their findings show that Chagas' disease, a parasitical infection that plagues Central and South America now, has been around for quite a while.
Felipe Guhl of the University of the Andes in Bogota, working with colleagues in the United States and Italy, found genetic evidence of the parasites in mummies from the Atacama desert in Peru.

"Our results indicate that human residents at coastal sites in southwestern South America suffered from American trypanosomiasis (Chagas' disease) as long as 4,000 years ago," they wrote in a letter to the Lancet medical journal.
Chagas' disease, caused by the Trypanosoma cruzi protozoa, affects 18 to 20 million Latin Americans today. Several insects carry the bug, which is passed on in their droppings.
Victims are usually infected as infants and it can be decades before any symptoms appear.
It can cause heart muscle failure, leading to heart attacks, and abnormalities in the oesophagus and colon causing trouble swallowing and constipation.
